candidates.title: Physics Basis of the Infinity Two Fusion Power Plant — JPP Collection
candidates.notes: Identified 6 papers in series (E65, E76, E83, E86, E88, E94). E86 (breeder blanket) mentions 'thermal efficiencies >30%' but no explicit value. No paper in the collection covers balance-of-plant or power conversion efficiency specifically.

candidates.title: Overview of the Helios Design: A Practical Planar Coil Stellarator Fusion Power Plant (Thea Energy)
candidates.notes: Direct stellarator BOP analog. Confirms: 40% Rankine thermal efficiency, 1.1 GW thermal from 958 MW fusion (blanket multiplier ~1.15), 438 MWe gross, 390 MWe net, steam superheated to 635°C. Low recirculating power consistent with steady-state stellarator advantage. Freely accessible on arXiv.

candidates.title: An optimized power conversion system for a stellarator-based nuclear fusion power plant
candidates.notes: ScienceDirect abstract only; full text requires institutional access. Likely paywalled. Skipped in favor of open-access Helios paper.

candidates.title: ARIES-CS Compact Stellarator Power Plant — IAEA FEC 2006

gaps_attempted.notes: No Infinity Two–specific thermal efficiency value published. Helios analog (Thea Energy, another planar-coil stellarator) confirms 40% Rankine cycle efficiency for a comparable stellarator with 1.1 GW thermal output, 635°C steam. Provides independent constraint on the 38–42% implied range in the analysis. Gap remains partial — Infinity Two thermal efficiency is still derivable, not directly published.

candidates.title: Power and particle exhaust for the Infinity Two fusion pilot plant — J. Plasma Phys. 2025
candidates.notes: Full paper accessible (open access). Explicitly states: 'The baseline scenario of Infinity Two includes 20 MW of auxiliary power.' This is the ECRH auxiliary heating power for the published baseline design. Confirms the upper bound (20 MW from Q=40) is also the design-point value.

candidates.title: The Infinity Two fusion pilot plant baseline plasma physics design (E76) — J. Plasma Phys. 2025
candidates.notes: Mentions '236 GHz gyrotrons with fundamental resonance at 8.42 T' (consistent with 9 T on-axis). Projects Q=40 at design density; notes Q=∞ (ignition) accessible at slightly higher density with 1.5 GW fusion. Does not explicitly state total ECRH power in MW in accessible excerpt. Full text would require extraction.
